summary: OpenRemote is an open-source Internet of Things platform that provides asset management, edge gateway capabilities, and data visualisation. It includes rule engines using flow-based and conditional logic to automate interactions between connected devices and services. Written in Java and distributed under the AGPL-3.0 licence, it is designed to help you aggregate and control disparate connected hardware.
goodFor: It is a solid fit if you need a self-hosted platform to monitor and control heterogeneous IoT deployments with custom automation rules.
watchOut: The AGPL-3.0 licence requires you to release the source code of your modifications if you offer the software as a network service, which may restrict commercial usage. Additionally, setting up complex flow rules and edge gateways typically demands a steep learning curve.
deployNotes: Because the application is built with Java, you will usually need to allocate sufficient JVM memory and pair it with a persistent storage volume for your device data. It is also standard practice to place the service behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
